text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/12 - 01 - Essay
A calendar gives plans a place in time.
Pexels · 20657557
Making room for what matters
Everyday change depends on more than willpower. Meaningful routines are more likely to last when environments
reduce friction and expectations remain flexible enough to preserve the value of the activity itself.
Reducing friction makes a valued choice easier to begin. A notebook left open or reading materials prepared in
advance removes a small but repeated obstacle. Someone who wants to write after dinner, for instance, can prepare
a quiet space before the evening becomes crowded with other demands.
Flexible expectations protect the purpose behind the routine. A reader who treats a daily page target as compulsory
may lose the pleasure that motivated the habit. Allowing a shorter session on a demanding day preserves
engagement without making measurement the activity’s sole justification.
What I find useful is therefore a balance between supportive structure and permission to adapt. The former eases the
first step; the latter preserves meaning when circumstances change. Intentionality works best when it supports
ordinary life rather than demanding perfect predictability.
BUILD YOUR OWN · Establish two conditions for lasting routines. Explain reduced friction and flexible expectations with
distinct examples. Synthesize their complementary roles. Follow the main idea through two supported points. The conclusion
brings both points together without adding a new reason.
What risk does the third paragraph identify? (Model: Measuring and optimising an activity can displace the enjoyment or
meaning that originally made it valuable.)
